ring_rearm_regression.input: The same PM4 fixture is written as three separate CP_RB_WPTR MMIO updates.
ring_rearm_regression.synchronization: The test waits for the guest read-pointer writeback after each update before writing the next batch.
ring_rearm_regression.observed: All three read-pointer milestones were reached and all three batches produced a Vulkan presenter submission.

diagnostic_readback.scope: Synthetic renderer diagnostic only; not retail output or parity evidence.

interrupt_abi_review.sdk_entry: VdSetGraphicsInterruptCallback_entry converts mapped user_data with guest_address() before SetInterruptCallback.
interrupt_abi_review.sdk_dispatch: The SDK dispatches {source, stored_user_data} to ExecuteInterrupt.
interrupt_abi_review.process2_dispatch: The plugin stores that guest user_data unchanged and dispatches {source, stored_callback_data}.
interrupt_abi_review.conclusion: The Process 2 wrapper preserves the r4 user_data value; this code path does not explain a null nested guest field at object+10900.

limits: The smoke proves the ring worker can re-arm after each consumed batch when a new guest WPTR is written; it does not prove why the retail guest stops writing WPTR after its startup batches.
The fixture uses synthetic vertex and resource inputs and makes no claim about retail pixels.
The Redmi Note 8 Pro retail application remains black with no later PM4 batch in its current runtime log; guest-side progress remains under Process 1 investigation.
